name: Serge and Dining Room
description: Serge came to the school dining room and discovered that there is a big queue here. There are $$$m$$$ pupils in the queue. He's not sure now if he wants to wait until the queue will clear, so he wants to know which dish he will receive if he does. As Serge is very tired, he asks you to compute it instead of him. Initially there are $$$n$$$ dishes with costs $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$. As you already know, there are the queue of $$$m$$$ pupils who have $$$b_1, \ldots, b_m$$$ togrogs respectively (pupils are enumerated by queue order, i.e the first pupil in the queue has $$$b_1$$$ togrogs and the last one has $$$b_m$$$ togrogs) Pupils think that the most expensive dish is the most delicious one, so every pupil just buys the most expensive dish for which he has money (every dish has a single copy, so when a pupil has bought it nobody can buy it later), and if a pupil doesn't have money for any dish, he just leaves the queue (so brutal capitalism...) But money isn't a problem at all for Serge, so Serge is buying the most expensive dish if there is at least one remaining. Moreover, Serge's school has a very unstable economic situation and the costs of some dishes or number of togrogs of some pupils can change. More formally, you must process $$$q$$$ queries: change $$$a_i$$$ to $$$x$$$. It means that the price of the $$$i$$$-th dish becomes $$$x$$$ togrogs. change $$$b_i$$$ to $$$x$$$. It means that the $$$i$$$-th pupil in the queue has $$$x$$$ togrogs now. Nobody leaves the queue during those queries because a saleswoman is late. After every query, you must tell Serge price of the dish which he will buy if he has waited until the queue is clear, or $$$-1$$$ if there are no dishes at this point, according to rules described above.
input_specification: The first line contains integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \leq n, m \leq 300\ 000$$$) — number of dishes and pupils respectively. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^{6}$$$) — elements of array $$$a$$$. The third line contains $$$m$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_{m}$$$ ($$$1 \leq b_i \leq 10^{6}$$$) — elements of array $$$b$$$. The fourth line conatins integer $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \leq q \leq 300\ 000$$$) — number of queries. Each of the following $$$q$$$ lines contains as follows: if a query changes price of some dish, it contains $$$1$$$, and two integers $$$i$$$ and $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$, $$$1 \leq x \leq 10^{6}$$$), what means $$$a_i$$$ becomes $$$x$$$. if a query changes number of togrogs of some pupil, it contains $$$2$$$, and two integers $$$i$$$ and $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \leq i \leq m$$$, $$$1 \leq x \leq 10^{6}$$$), what means $$$b_i$$$ becomes $$$x$$$.
output_specification: For each of $$$q$$$ queries prints the answer as the statement describes, the answer of the $$$i$$$-th query in the $$$i$$$-th line (the price of the dish which Serge will buy or $$$-1$$$ if nothing remains)
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1179C — Serge and Dining Room [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
